capability: Evaluate the FFT Maxwellian dispersion approximation with its default order and declared failure contract.
operation: evaluate the FFT Maxwellian dispersion function
discovery.boundary: Real axis is accepted; exponential continuation overflow raises.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: ValueError for nonfinite/empty phase points, invalid integer order or unsupported pole count.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Fixed approximation has no iterative convergence claim.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No partial result after a failed call.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: FloatingPointError if w or the final scaled Z exceeds finite float64 range; finite w alone does not establish representable Z.

scope: Default and explicit order, scalar/matrix shapes, reflection, normalization, positive imaginary axis overflow regression.
80-digit mpmath equation grid and 70-digit independent Gaussian Cauchy integrals.
Finite w but overflowing scaled Z fails explicitly, including mixed matrices and both sides of the mathematical negative-imaginary-axis scaling threshold.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Bounded to the declared relation: Weideman rational FFT expansion with erfcx on imaginary axis. Evidence: test_generalized_dispersion_faddeeva_variants.py, test_generalized_dispersion_faddeeva_independent.py, test_generalized_dispersion_fft_scaling.py (13 recorded test functions; bound-file coverage; independent analytic/high-precision oracle); the contract example ran. Excluded scope: A guaranteed global error bound; An arbitrary distribution response.
known_limitations: Fixed truncation error depends on phase point and order.
The independent analytic comparison does not replace an external experimental reference.

summary: Evaluate the FFT Maxwellian dispersion approximation with its default order and declared failure contract.

identity.definition: Weideman rational FFT expansion with erfcx on imaginary axis.
identity.boundary: Real axis is accepted; exponential continuation overflow raises.

supported: Finite nonempty scalar or array input; shape preserved.
preconditions: All phase values and computed results fit complex128.

inputs.name: order
inputs.description: Rational truncation or pole count. Explicit None is invalid.
inputs.constraints: Any positive integer order. Boolean rejected.

example.code:
from scirel.kinetic import evaluate_maxwellian_fft
import numpy as np
r=evaluate_maxwellian_fft(0.2+0.7j)
assert np.isfinite(r["Z"])
example.expected: Observed PASS: Finite complex response at the effective order.

references: Weideman (1994), Computation of the Complex Error Function, doi:10.1137/0731077
Xie (2013), Generalized Plasma Dispersion Function, arXiv:1305.6476
